_note: Every scored number is recomputed by eval/ from raw predictions (u0 and solution sensitivities) on instances the evaluator holds; the paper reports its accuracy claims graphically or verbally, so the proposed-method primary values below encode those statements (1.0 = 'sensitivities consistent with / match the reference derivative', 0.0 = 'completely off'). Rank: each metric's improvement over the reference run in scoring/scores_test.json, taken in its higher_is_better direction, times |coefficient| and the experiment weight, divided by the metric's spread across ranked attempts.

pendulum_sensitivity_accuracy.description: Paper Sec. 5.1 / App. A.10 highly-parametric pendulum-on-cart OCP (N=50, T=2, nx=4, nu=1, n_theta=1; theta = cart mass entering cost, RK4 dynamics and the path constraint |theta*p|<=1.5), tau_min = 0. Hidden instances: theta in [0.6,1.5] and the paper's initial state (0, pi/2, 0, 0) or a perturbed one; each ships the warm start of the paper's sweep (solution on the same branch at theta -/+ 1e-3). Instances whose u0 sits at the force bound (trivially zero sensitivity) are excluded. Score: d u0 / d theta against an independent IPOPT + Newton + implicit-function-theorem ground truth. Core claim: exact-Hessian IFT sensitivities are correct (consistent with finite differences), Gauss-Newton-Hessian ones are completely off (Remark 3, Fig. 2).

frac_sens_accurate.description: Fraction of instances whose reported u0 is correct (relative error <= 1e-5) and whose d u0/d theta has relative error <= 1e-4 (error / max(1, |true|)). Missing, malformed or non-finite entries count as failures.

mean_log10_sens_rel_err.description: Mean over instances of log10 relative sensitivity error clipped to [-10, 0]; instances with a wrong or missing solution count as 0 (worst).

frac_u0_accurate.description: Constraint: fraction of instances whose reported optimal u0 matches the ground-truth solution on the warm-start branch (relative error <= 1e-5). A method may not change the problem (e.g. smooth it) to make sensitivities easier.

pendulum_sensitivity_accuracy._paper_statement: Sec. 5.1: 'The solution sensitivities obtained with tau_min = 0 are consistent with the ones obtained by finite differences, while the results obtained by the IFT approach with a Gauss-Newton Hessian approximation are completely off.' No numeric error is reported.

_legacy_prior_reproduction_value.note: Single-point error of an earlier reproduction against its own finite difference; not a paper number and no longer scored.

pendulum_smoothed_sensitivity.description: Same pendulum OCP solved as the smoothed interior-point KKT system (paper eq. 10/23) with tau_min in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} (Fig. 2 uses 1e-3 and 1e-2): every one-sided inequality h_i <= 0 satisfies mu_i*h_i = -tau_min, equalities stay exact, stage costs scaled by dt = T/N. Score: derivative of the smoothed solution map u0(theta; tau_min) against the independent ground truth. Claim (Thm. 3, Remark 2): the IFT on the smoothed system gives the correct sensitivities of the smoothed solution map.

frac_sens_accurate.description: Fraction of instances with correct smoothed u0 (relative error <= 1e-5) and smoothed-map sensitivity relative error <= 1e-4.

mean_log10_sens_rel_err.description: Mean clipped log10 relative error of the smoothed-map sensitivity (worst value 0 for wrong/missing solutions).

frac_u0_accurate.description: Constraint: fraction of instances whose reported u0 solves the requested smoothed problem.

pendulum_smoothed_sensitivity._paper_statement: Remark 2 / App. A.3: 'the proposed method provides the correct sensitivities of the smoothed solution map'; Fig. 2 shows the smoothed sensitivities for tau_min in {1e-3, 1e-2} without a numeric accuracy.

bounded_lqr_adjoint_accuracy.description: Paper Sec. 5.2 / App. A.11 bounded LQR (N=20, nx=8, nu=4, n_theta=248 = vec(A), vec(B), b, vec(H) column-major; A = I + 0.2*M, B, b, x0 standard normal, H = I; u_max in {1, 1e4}). Score: the adjoint sensitivity d(seed . u0)/d theta (all 248 parameters, hidden random seed on u0) against an exact active-set QP ground truth. Instances with every u0 component at its bound (trivially zero adjoint) are excluded. Claim (App. A.11): acados' solutions and adjoint sensitivities match those of the independent solvers. The paper's speed-ups are wall-clock and therefore not scored here.

frac_sens_accurate.description: Fraction of instances with correct u0 (max relative error <= 1e-5) and adjoint relative 2-norm error <= 1e-4 (error / max(1, ||true||)).

mean_log10_sens_rel_err.description: Mean clipped log10 relative adjoint error (worst value 0 for wrong/missing solutions).

frac_u0_accurate.description: Constraint: fraction of instances whose reported u0 is the QP solution.

bounded_lqr_adjoint_accuracy._paper_statement: App. A.11: 'for u_max = 1e4 the solvers acados, mpc.pytorch and cvxpygen converge to the same solution and the adjoint solution sensitivities match ... for u_max = 1.0, the solutions obtained with acados and cvxpygen match, while mpc.pytorch fails to converge.'

_paper_table1_timings_ms.note: Paper Table 1 (CPU, n_batch = 128, ms; multiples of acados in the paper). Kept unchanged for context; wall-clock time is not scored in this gym.

bounded_lqr_adjoint_accuracy._paper_fig3_chain: Sec. 5.3: a single adjoint sensitivity is about 2.5x faster than the full forward Jacobian on the chain example (N=40, n_theta=113); wall-clock, not scored.
